solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Where policeman’s first introduced to truncheon work? (3,4)

definitions.text: Where policeman’s first introduced to truncheon work?

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of 'policeman'
the P is put inside the truncheon

blocks.note: a cosh is a short club
first letter of policeman, placed inside COSH
op = opus, a work

annotation.surface: A new constable is handed a truncheon on the first day at the station.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read straight, it describes the police station where a new officer first meets a truncheon. COP SHOP is slang for a police station.
annotation.definitionFit: A cop shop is informal slang for a police station, where policemen are given their kit.

entries.clue: Youngster on American island (4)

blocks.note: a cub is a young animal, or a junior Scout
A = American, a standard abbreviation

annotation.surface: A young person living on an island off the United States.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed after, so CUB sits on top of A.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Cuba is one island among many, the largest in the Caribbean.

entries.clue: Wind getting up in film of the ocean (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read bottom to top, so GALE flips
the flipped wind goes inside the film

blocks.note: pic = picture, a film
a gale is a strong wind; reversed to ELAG and put inside PIC

annotation.surface: A strong wind rises during a sea documentary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind getting up' reads like weather in the film; really 'getting up' reverses GALE in this down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Pelagic describes the open ocean and the creatures that live in it.

entries.clue: Place to stay in centre of Medellin (5)

indicators.note: takes the middle two letters of the eight-letter Medellin

blocks.note: in and hot both mean fashionable
MED-EL-LIN: the middle two letters

annotation.surface: A traveller looks for somewhere to stay in the middle of the Colombian city of Medellin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word joining 'Place to stay' to the city; it is actually HOT, as in 'the in thing'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hotel offers rooms where travellers stay the night.

entries.clue: Old man scowls after initially referencing Chambers (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming after means sitting later in the column, so LOURS goes below the R
takes the first letter of 'referencing'

blocks.note: pa = father, one's old man
first letter of referencing
to lour (or lower) is to frown or scowl

annotation.surface: A grumpy old man frowns as he looks something up in the Chambers dictionary.
annotation.walkthrough: Chambers is a famous British dictionary, which is what 'referencing Chambers' makes you picture; here it is just rooms.
annotation.definitionFit: Parlours are sitting rooms, and chambers are rooms.

entries.clue: Celebrity mate with new business (5-2)

blocks.note: a star is a celebrity
to tup is what a ram does to mate with a ewe

annotation.surface: A famous person and a friend go into business together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'mate' reads as a friend; it is the verb, and TUP is the farmyard word for a ram mating.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the usual term for a young company just launched, often in tech.

entries.clue: Regularly supply wood for blaze (6)

indicators.note: takes every other letter: S, P, L from SuPpLy

blocks.note: letters 1, 3 and 5 of SUPPLY
ash is a tree and its timber

annotation.surface: Someone keeps a fire going by bringing firewood at regular intervals.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'blaze' a fire; it is the verb used of headlines, as when news is blazed or splashed across a front page.
annotation.definitionFit: To splash a story is to blaze it prominently across a newspaper.

entries.clue: Legendary outlaw’s lover ditching male and seizing day (9)

indicators.note: the M for male is dropped from MARIAN
what remains takes THUR inside it

blocks.note: Maid Marian, the sweetheart of the outlaw Robin Hood
M = male, removed to leave ARIAN
THUR = Thursday, placed inside what is left

annotation.surface: Robin Hood's girlfriend leaves a man and grabs her chance of a day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Legendary outlaw' reads as a phrase, pointing at Robin Hood; the definition is 'Legendary' alone, and it moves the legend from Sherwood to Camelot.
annotation.definitionFit: Arthurian means belonging to the legends of King Arthur.

entries.clue: Couple married in bustling Soweto (7)

indicators.note: M goes inside the rearranged letters
the letters of SOWETO rush about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, rearranged to TWOSOE
M = married, as in genealogies; it sits inside the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: A pair get married in the busy South African township of Soweto.
annotation.walkthrough: Soweto is a large township near Johannesburg; its six letters plus M make the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: two people seen together as a pair.

entries.clue: Daily bread for Buffalo Bill? (5,5)

blocks.note: the surface means food eaten each day; the setter means a daily is a newspaper, so paper, and bread is slang for money
Buffalo Bill Cody was a Wild West showman, but a bill is also a banknote, and old US notes carried a buffalo

annotation.surface: What the Wild West showman Buffalo Bill ate every day.
annotation.walkthrough: Read it again: 'daily' is a newspaper, so paper; 'bread' is slang for money; a 'bill' is a banknote, and US notes have carried the buffalo.
annotation.definitionFit: Paper money is banknotes: bills, or bread in slang, made of paper like a daily.

entries.clue: In Kabul, are Taliban retreating on both sides? (9)

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the words that follow
going backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: kabuL ARE TALIBan, read backwards

annotation.surface: A question about whether the Taliban are pulling back from Kabul on two fronts.
annotation.walkthrough: The run starts at the last letter of Kabul and ends inside Taliban; read right to left it spells the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Bilateral means involving or affecting both sides.

entries.clue: Soldiers left Lima, fleeing from floozy (5)

indicators.note: the L and L run out of the word

blocks.note: a trollop is a disreputable woman
L = left, removed
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet; the second L to go

annotation.surface: Soldiers abandon the Peruvian capital, running away from a loose woman.
annotation.walkthrough: Lima looks like the city; it is the radio code word for the letter L.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a troop is a group, so it stands for the plural 'Soldiers'.

entries.clue: Drollery when facing suspension? (7,6)

blocks.note: drollery is dry wit, and the surface keeps it light
the surface suggests being suspended from a job; the setter means being suspended by the neck

annotation.surface: Someone cracks jokes while awaiting suspension from work or school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suspension' suggests being barred from work; here it is being hanged, and jokes made facing the noose are gallows humour.
annotation.definitionFit: Gallows humour is grim joking in the face of death or disaster, as by someone about to be hanged.

entries.clue: Walking stick of grim Germanic character (10)

blocks.note: black as in black humour: grim
thorn is the runic letter þ, used in Old English and Norse

annotation.surface: A cane belonging to a gloomy German.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Germanic character' suggests a gloomy person; it is a letter of the old Germanic runic alphabet.
annotation.definitionFit: A blackthorn is a walking stick cut from the blackthorn shrub, the Irish shillelagh.

entries.clue: Cross dons can rapidly empty chat room (8)

indicators.note: LOO puts on CUT like a garment, wrapping around it
remove the insides of rapidly, leaving R and Y

blocks.note: can and loo are both slang for a lavatory
to cut across something is to cross it; CUT goes inside LOO
RapidlY with the middle removed

annotation.surface: Angry academics quickly clear the common room.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross dons' paints annoyed university teachers; 'dons' is the verb, putting on. A locutory is a room in a monastery where talk is allowed.
annotation.definitionFit: A locutory is a parlour in a monastery set aside for conversation.

entries.clue: Played other tune to that (9)

indicators.note: the letters are performed in a different arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: A musician switched to a different melody.
annotation.walkthrough: The musical surface disguises an old-fashioned legal word.
annotation.definitionFit: Thereunto is a formal word meaning to that thing.

entries.clue: Eloquent Roman commander-in-chief meeting hero without aspiration (6)

indicators.note: an aspirate is the H sound, so HERO drops its H

blocks.note: CIC is the abbreviation
loses its H to give ERO

annotation.surface: A silver-tongued Roman general meets a hero who has no ambition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without aspiration' reads as lacking ambition; in phonetics aspiration is the breathy H, so HERO is spoken as a Cockney would.
annotation.definitionFit: Cicero was Rome's greatest orator.

entries.clue: Retired chap and ex-PM almost go to war (2,6)

indicators.note: withdrawn, going backwards: BOD becomes DOB
the last letter is cut off ATTLEE

blocks.note: bod is British slang for a person, a chap
Clement Attlee, Labour Prime Minister 1945-51, minus his last E

annotation.surface: A pensioner and a former prime minister nearly start a war.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retired chap' paints a pensioner; 'retired' means drawn back, reversing BOD.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: doing battle means engaging in fighting, as nations going to war do.

entries.clue: Skips about naked in motor home (6)

indicators.note: stripped of its outer covering: the first and last letters go

blocks.note: to scamper is to skip about playfully; naked, the word loses its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Someone prances around nude inside their motor home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skips about' looks like two ideas, perhaps a word around another; it is a single synonym, SCAMPERS, then stripped bare.
annotation.definitionFit: A camper is a motor home, a van fitted out for living in.

entries.clue: Short people collectively bolstered by current swimsuit style (7)

indicators.note: the last letter of MANKIND is cut
in a down clue, the I is placed beneath as a support

blocks.note: mankind is the human race; cut short to MANKIN
I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: Small people, backed by fashion, take up a new style of swimwear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short people' suggests small people; 'Short' is an instruction applying to the phrase 'people collectively'.
annotation.definitionFit: A mankini is a skimpy one-piece men's swimsuit, made famous by the film Borat.

entries.clue: Once rich, fancy a Rolls Royce (8)

indicators.note: elaborate, rearranged: the letters are made into something fancier

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone formerly wealthy still dreams of owning a Rolls-Royce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'fancy' reads as the verb to desire; it is the adjective meaning elaborate, signalling a rearrangement.
annotation.definitionFit: The Corniche was a Rolls-Royce convertible model built from 1971.

entries.clue: Number of joint head of faculty read out (7)

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the sound of the phrase gives the answer

blocks.note: a co-dean shares the post of dean, the head of a faculty

annotation.surface: A figure is read out for the shared head of a university department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number' is the painkiller sense, something that numbs, not a figure. 'Joint' could mean a cannabis cigarette, fitting the drug; here it means shared.
annotation.definitionFit: Codeine is a painkilling drug, something that numbs.

entries.clue: Sample of paunchy presenter’s perfume (6)

indicators.note: a small portion is taken from the words that follow

blocks.note: paunCHY PREsenter

annotation.surface: A test sniff of the scent worn by a pot-bellied TV host.
annotation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of paunchy and the start of presenter.
annotation.definitionFit: Chypre is a family of perfumes built on oakmoss and citrus, named after Cyprus.

entries.clue: Easily touched, offer last of our warm blankets (6-7)

indicators.note: takes the final letter of 'our'
HEATED covers the R like a blanket

blocks.note: to tender is to offer
heated = warm, wrapped around the R
last letter of our

annotation.surface: Someone sentimental offers the last of their warm blankets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'blankets' reads as bedding in the surface; it is the verb to cover.
annotation.definitionFit: Tender-hearted people are easily moved to sympathy, easily touched.

entries.clue: Lay lisping in minimal underwear (5)

indicators.note: a lisp turns the S sound into TH

blocks.note: a lay is a song or ballad; lisped, its S becomes TH

annotation.surface: Someone lies about with a lisp, wearing next to nothing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lay' looks like a verb; it is the old poetic noun for a song.
annotation.definitionFit: A thong is a skimpy undergarment with a string back.

entries.clue: Extremely “biddable” nationalist turned out to be corrupt (4)

indicators.note: take the extremes, the first and last letters, of each word

blocks.note: first and last letters of biddable
first and last letters of nationalist

annotation.surface: A supposedly docile nationalist politician proved to be on the take.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' reads as an intensifier; it works on both following words. Bent is British slang for corrupt, especially of police.
annotation.definitionFit: Bent is British slang for dishonest or corrupt.

entries.clue: Nothing for you in marriage — it causes tears (5)

indicators.note: the O stands in place of U

blocks.note: a marriage is a union
O = zero, nothing
U is text-speak for you; O replaces it in UNION

annotation.surface: A marriage without anything for you in it ends in tears.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a sad marriage; the tears are the watery eyes caused by chopping an onion.
annotation.definitionFit: Cutting an onion releases a gas that makes the eyes water.

entries.clue: Frequent fighting in seaport (9)

indicators.note: letters at war are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Brawls often break out in a harbour town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frequent' looks like an adjective describing the fighting; it is the verb, to visit regularly. 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
annotation.definitionFit: To patronise a shop or pub is to frequent it as a customer.

entries.clue: Disgusting racket stopped by order (7)

indicators.note: OM plugs the gap inside NOISE

blocks.note: a racket is a loud noise
OM = Order of Merit, a British honour

annotation.surface: An awful din is halted by a command.
annotation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a command; it is an honour, the Order of Merit. Noisome means foul-smelling, not noisy, despite the look of it.
annotation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of smells.

entries.clue: Gide novel is in French and most intense (7)

indicators.note: new, so the letters of GIDE are made new
translate 'is' into French

blocks.note: anagram of GIDE
est is French for is

annotation.surface: A novel by the French writer André Gide is praised as his most intense.
annotation.walkthrough: André Gide was a French novelist, so 'Gide novel' looks like one of his books; 'novel' is an anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Edgiest means most tense, intense or cutting-edge.
